Doing this was literally called “salting the lantern,” and in railroad circles the expression soon spread figuratively to mean “making the last small, practical preparation before going to work.”  The phrase is documented in Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen’s Magazine (1903), CB&Q and C&NW rule-books from the 1900s, and a handful of memoirs of railroaders from the period.  Those early trade sources leave little doubt about where it started, but the saying never became common outside railroad talk, so although the origin is well established in that niche, it has only spotty currency in general English today.
